title: Maui's Family Across Island Accounts
subtitle: Names and kinship vary across the collected versions

learningObjectives.text: What does the Hawaiian chant name as Maui's father's name?
What does Westervelt say varies among the island accounts?

family.work: Legends of Ma-Ui, a Demi God of Polynesia and of his Mother Hina
family.author: W. D. Westervelt
family.locator: Chapter I · MAUI'S HOME; Chapter I · MAUI'S HOME, normalized characters 2031-2317
family.excerpt: In the Hawaiian chant, Akalana was the name of his father. In other groups this was the name by which his mother was known. Kanaloa, the god, is sometimes known as the father of Maui. In Hawaii Hina was his mother. Elsewhere Ina, or Hina, was the grandmother, from whom he secured fire.
family.note: Verbatim prose from Westervelt's early twentieth-century English compilation. Retain the named island/version; this is not a direct transcription of one oral performance.

narrativeBlocks.title: One hero, different genealogies
narrativeBlocks.body: Westervelt's collection notes that accounts vary: in the Hawaiian chant Akalana is Maui's father, while other versions give the name to his mother or connect Hina with his grandmother.

narrativeBlocks.title: Kinship depends on the island version
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Westervelt's English compilation (whitespace normalized): “In the Hawaiian chant, Akalana was the name of his father. In other groups this was the name by which his mother was known. Kanaloa, the god, is sometimes known as the father of Maui. In Hawaii Hina was his mother. Elsewhere Ina, or Hina, was the grandmother, from whom he secured fire.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The compiler compares traditions
narrativeBlocks.body: Westervelt's 1910s volume brings together material identified with Hawaii, New Zealand, Hervey, Tahiti, and other islands. The compiler's comparison is not one single Polynesian canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: A modern compilation
narrativeBlocks.body: W. D. Westervelt wrote in English and collated island accounts and chants. This source is not a direct translation of one ancient manuscript or one unmediated oral performance.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep the variant label
narrativeBlocks.body: When retelling Maui's family story, name the Hawaiian chant or the other island account rather than merging their genealogies.
